source_name: BQK — Rregullore mbi Statistikat e Instrumenteve të Pagesave (Regulation on Payment Instrument Statistics)
why_relevant: The legal instrument that defines exactly which payment-instrument statistics banks must report to the CBK, with reporting templates and frequency. It is the schema key: it tells the collector which series must exist (cards by type, ATM/POS counts, e-banking users) even when the published tables are terse.

source_name: BQK — Rregullore për Sistemin e Pagesave Ndërbankare (interbank payment system regulation, SPN/KIPS)
why_relevant: Defines the national interbank clearing/settlement system (SPN, a.k.a. KIPS — the hybrid clearing+settlement system) — participants, session structure, transaction types. Essential for interpreting KIS/ATS volume series and for naming the actors that generate them.

source_name: BQK — Rregullore për Instrumentet e Pagesave Elektronike (electronic payment instruments regulation)
why_relevant: Sets conditions for issuing/using electronic payment instruments and the reporting obligations attached to their use — defines the population of card and e-money issuers whose data feeds the card statistics.

source_name: BQK — Këshilli Kombëtar i Pagesave (National Payments Council) minutes and materials
why_relevant: NPC meeting minutes carry payment-infrastructure and payment-service statistics presented to the industry (e.g. non-cash transactions per capita against NSSVP targets) — often the earliest public release of a given year's terminal/instrument numbers, in both sq and en.

source_name: BQK — Strategjia Kombëtare për Pagesat me Vlera të Vogla (National Retail Payments Strategy, NSSVP 2021-2026)
why_relevant: Strategy document and its progress reporting set quantified targets (e.g. non-cash payments per capita) and therefore publish baseline and monitoring series on cards, terminals, e-banking and cash usage — a structured indicator framework rather than raw tables.

source_name: BQK — Raporti Vjetor i BQK-së (CBK Annual Report), payment-system chapter
why_relevant: The annual report contains a dedicated payment-systems chapter reporting interbank system (KIPS/SPN) transaction counts and values, account numbers, e-banking access and e-money payments — a reliable annual anchor when the departmental tables lag.

source_name: BQK — Raporti i Informatave Mujore të Sistemit Financiar (Monthly Financial System Information Report)
why_relevant: Monthly publication running since January 2014 covering banking, microfinance, insurance and pensions; the highest-frequency CBK release and the place to check whether any payment-instrument or account indicators are carried at monthly cadence.

source_name: BQK — Serbian-language payment system portal (Platni sistem)
why_relevant: Mirror of the payment-systems section in Serbian; occasionally exposes documents or wording (e.g. 'kartice', 'bankomati', 'POS terminali') not surfacing under Albanian queries, and is a required leg of bilingual coverage for XK.

source_name: IMF Financial Access Survey (FAS) — Kosovo ATM/POS/geographical outreach series
why_relevant: Kosovo reports to the FAS, giving an internationally standardised, machine-readable annual series for ATMs and POS terminals (country-wide and per 100,000 adults) back to ~2005 — an independent cross-check on CBK figures and a fallback when CBK PDFs are unparsable.

source_name: FRED / St. Louis Fed — Kosovo ATM count series (KOSFCACNUM)
why_relevant: Clean, versioned, API-accessible mirror of the IMF FAS Kosovo ATM series; the lowest-friction way to keep a continuously updated terminal-count baseline without fighting the CBK's bot defences.

source_name: World Bank Global Findex 2025 — Kosovo microdata and indicators
why_relevant: Demand-side counterpart to CBK supply-side statistics: account ownership, card ownership and use, digital payments made/received, and cash reliance for Kosovo — the only comparable survey evidence on cash usage behaviour.

source_name: Commercial bank annual reports (ProCredit, Raiffeisen Kosovo, NLB Banka, TEB, BKT Kosova)
why_relevant: Issuer-side disclosure: individual banks report their own ATM fleet, POS acquiring network, card portfolio and e/m-banking user counts. Aggregating them gives a bottom-up cross-check on CBK totals and, uniquely, market-share splits the CBK does not publish.

source_name: Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës (Kosovo Banking Association)
why_relevant: Industry body that aggregates member-bank information and publishes sector material (including work on digital/e-banking services in Kosovo); a likely route to sector-level card and channel data and to industry events where terminal statistics are presented.

source_name: Agjencia e Statistikave të Kosovës (ASK) — ICT usage survey in households/enterprises
why_relevant: The national statistics office's ICT survey measures internet use and online/e-banking behaviour among individuals and enterprises — demand-side context for e-banking and mobile-banking user counts, and independent of the CBK reporting chain.

source_name: BQK — KosGIRO scheme documentation (legacy direct-debit/bill payment scheme)
why_relevant: KosGIRO is the domestic bill-payment/direct-debit scheme; its documentation names the scheme, participants and transaction types that appear as line items in CBK payment-instrument statistics — necessary vocabulary for parsing the instrument breakdowns.

source_name: env2.bqk-kos.org — legacy/staging mirror of CBK document repository
why_relevant: A second CBK host surfaced in search results serving historical Monthly Statistics Bulletins from the /repository/docs/ tree. If it is less aggressively defended than the main site, it is a viable collection path for historical payment tables.

source_name: Printec Group — corporate site (solutions, ATM/POS, country presence)
why_relevant: Printec is a CEE-wide ATM/self-service and POS integrator that operates in the Western Balkans and has publicly claimed Kosovo bank work (BPB ATM network renewal). Its solutions and country pages point to which Kosovo institutions run which self-service infrastructure.

source_name: Printec Blog — CEE ATM & EFT-POS landscape series (per-country penetration figures)
why_relevant: Printec publishes recurring CEE ATM/POS landscape posts with per-country penetration metrics; Kosovo appears with explicit figures (e.g. ATM units per million capita), giving vendor-side estimates that predate or complement CBK statistics.

source_name: Printec Group social channels (Facebook/LinkedIn) — customer win announcements
why_relevant: Vendor social posts carry deployment announcements that never reach the corporate site — e.g. an explicit post that Printec helped BPB Bank in Kosovo renew its ATM network by replacing the fleet. Names the Kosovo institution and the technology refresh event.

source_name: Payten (Asseco SEE group) — news & customer deployment announcements
why_relevant: Payten is the ASEE group payments arm operating ~600k POS and ~9,500 ATMs across 16 countries incl. the Western Balkans. Its news page quantifies terminal deliveries and go-lives per bank (e.g. Credins Bank Albania POS delivery), and is the most likely place a Kosovo POS/ATM managed-services win would first be quantified.

source_name: Asseco SEE (ASEE) — group structure and company contacts, incl. Asseco SEE sh.p.k. Prishtina
why_relevant: Confirms a registered Kosovo operating entity (Asseco SEE sh.p.k., Lidhja e Pejes 177, Prishtina), which is the local delivery vehicle for card systems, switches and ATM/POS services. Establishes the actor to track in Kosovo procurement, registry and bank vendor disclosures.

source_name: ASEE Investor relations / annual & quarterly reports (Warsaw Stock Exchange listed)
why_relevant: As a WSE-listed issuer, ASEE must disclose segment revenue and material contracts; its Payments segment reporting includes installed-base metrics (POS/ATM counts, transaction volumes) that can be traced regionally, and material Kosovo contracts would surface in current reports.

source_name: Compass Plus Technologies — customer success stories and newsroom (Quipu / Kosovo processing centre)
why_relevant: Compass Plus publishes a documented Kosovo deployment: Quipu's Kosovo card processing and personalisation centre running the TranzWare suite since 2004, with hard issuance numbers (6,000 contactless cards in under a month, 20,000 target). This is exactly the vendor-side quantification of Kosovo card infrastructure that precedes official statistics.

source_name: Quipu GmbH (ProCredit group IT/processing arm) — Kosovo processing & card personalisation centre
why_relevant: Quipu operates a processing and card personalisation centre physically in Kosovo serving ProCredit group banks; it is both an infrastructure operator and a vendor whose communications reveal Kosovo card issuance volumes, contactless migration timing and ATM/POS acquiring capability.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf — banking newsroom, DN Series and cash-recycling portfolio pages
why_relevant: One of the two global ATM OEMs whose hardware underpins Kosovo bank fleets (legacy Wincor Nixdorf estates are widespread in the Western Balkans). Its newsroom and cash-recycling collateral is where a Kosovo fleet refresh or recycler rollout would be announced with unit counts.

source_name: NCR Atleos / NCR Voyix — ATM and self-service press releases
why_relevant: The other global ATM OEM; NCR's post-spin ATM entity (Atleos) publishes fleet wins, ATM-as-a-Service deals and software (APTRA) migrations. Relevant as the alternate installed-base hypothesis for Kosovo bank fleets and for identifying the local partner/reseller serving Kosovo.

source_name: Halcom d.d. — e-banking vendor with declared Kosovo market entry
why_relevant: Halcom's corporate history states it won Kosovo and Albania as new markets and that Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo was the first user of its mobile bank — a dated, named Kosovo customer reference identifying the vendor behind a major Kosovo bank's digital channel.
